newsitem.title: USA: U.S. killer gets reprieve from electric chair.
newsitem.headline: U.S. killer gets reprieve from electric chair.

text.p: The Florida Supreme Court on Wednesday postponed the execution of a death row inmate until it hears arguments in September on the condition of the state's 74-year-old electric chair.

In a unanimous ruling, Florida's highest court postponed until at least Sept. 15 the execution of George Stano, who has confessed to killing 41 people and was scheduled to die for the slaying of a hitchhiker.

Stano is the second death row inmate to have his execution postponed following the fiery execution of Pedro Medina in March. State experts brought in to investigate after the incident blamed officials for not properly saturating a sponge used in the helmet.
The sponge caught fire, sending a 12-inch flame shooting out from Medina's head and filling the execution chamber with acrid smoke and the smell of burning flesh.
Last week, the court pulled the plug on the electric chair until September, postponing the execution of Leo Jones, who was convicted for the 1981 killing of a Jacksonville policeman.

Lawyers for Jones argued the chair, which has malfunctioned twice in seven years, is cruel and unusual punishment. The high court set oral arguments in that case for Sept. 15 to determine if the chair was working properly or should be turned off for good.
